title: FCC Commissioner Defends Clearance of GOP Senator's TV Appearance Amid Equal-Time Controversy
snippet: FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr rejected claims of selective enforcement after clearing a Republican senator's broadcast interview while raising regulatory concerns over a Democratic candidate's appearance.
content:
WASHINGTON — The Federal Communications Commission is facing fresh scrutiny over its application of broadcast equal-time rules following differing assessments of recent television appearances by political candidates.

FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr signaled that a recent broadcast interview featuring a sitting Republican senator met the criteria for standard news exemptions, contrasting it with a separate broadcast involving a Democratic candidate that drew regulatory red flags.

Navigating the Equal-Time Rule

Under federal communications law, broadcast stations that grant airtime to one political candidate must offer equal opportunity to rival contenders, unless the broadcast meets specific exemptions such as bona fide news interviews or news documentaries.

The distinction has drawn criticism from political observers who question the consistency of the agency's oversight, while FCC representatives maintain that regulatory determinations depend strictly on the format and context of individual broadcasts.
